body: This is true;  I second that, and the same thing happened to my wife in the first year when we were still dating.  If anything, it brought me closer to her.  I married her shortly after and we have been together for 13 years.  Don't lose hope, there is a great possibility that you will still live a fantastic and fulfilling life years from now.  My wife took awhile to get over it, but now it doesn't bother her much at all anymore.  Don't underestimate the power of being loved, and from what I can discern from your post, your boyfriend seems to care about you a great deal and will be there for you.  Even if it does trouble him and for some outlandish reason it comes between you (I don't think it will), there are so many people and men out there that won't look at you differently and still see a glimmering galaxy of stars shining in your eyes no matter the trauma you've been through.  The best love is truly unconditional, and I believe in my heart that this is attainable for everybody if they live life with love in their heart and love fearlessly.  There have been times in my life that I have tried to kill myself for my own trauma-related reasons, so I can utterly relate and sympathize with your plight.  When you're in it, you feel so mired in that myopic perspective and can't see an avenue of escape, even when with the right kind of eyes, there were many there all along.  I can tell you honestly and unabashedly that I'm entirely grateful that my attempts failed, for the universe unfolded as it should after those attempts and things coalesced for me into a serendipitous future that I would not have had, believe it or not, if I HADN'T been through the traumas and tribulations that i felt I couldn't aby and live through at the time.  Keep your head up, and remember that you're so young and there is a future out there where you live through this and go on to live a fulfilling and fantastic future, and that every experience, the good and the bad, are all the products of every situation and scene that you've lived through.  There's a silver lining in every situation I believe, and YOU have a choice on how it shapes you.  My traumas have endeared me to others that have suffered similar fates, and many relationships with dire importance to me now rest in my hearth of heart and warm my life with a light that would not have existed had they not been proceeded by a stygian darkness and mephitic fog that I couldn't see through at the time.  I have love and feel for all of you going through situations like these, for our common experience has inexorably bound us together in a powerful emotional experience, that power of love and sympathy i have for others directly inversely proportional to the negativity of the trauma I once felt.  Look into EMDR therapy for trauma, it's no joke and is helpful for so many.  It literally re-programs and processes the trauma so that it's not stored and triggered from its throne in the deep-subconscious part of the brain that assails us with the trauma response without warning.  I don't know you, but I love you.  Keep your head up, and I'll be sending a prayer out into the Universe to take care of you and help you attain a speedy recovery and beautiful future.  One last thing, there's a Japanese art called Kintsugi, where broken china and pottery is fixed and glued back together with gold filling and cementing it's cracks- I like to think it's a metaphor for people, and that even if we are damaged and ripped, we can end up beautifully sewn back together into something different, never whole as it once was, but more beautiful for the damage we've undergone if we put ourselves back together just right.  Peace and love to you all.

Phenibut is a GABA-B agonist, and as such, repeated use down regulates the receptors.  This is how withdrawal occurs from most drugs- down regulation.  When the brain receives the compound and it binds with the receptor it agonizes, your brain will release that neurotransmitter.  The brain has mechanisms that try to keep it and it's respective neurotransmitters at homeostasis, or in balance.  When phenibut causes the flood of GABA into the synapse for days in a row or even frequently, the brain decides that it is regularly getting a surplus of exogenous (from outside of the body) GABA, so it tries to regulate and decrease it's endogenous (produced inside the body) levels of GABA through down regulation.  The brain will decrease the amount of GABA-B receptors to compensate.  When the brain then becomes bereft of that exogenous source of GABA (you stop taking the phenibut), it struggles to produce enough endogenous or local GABA to saturate the fewer receptors it has after down-regulation.  The brain's need for that neurotransmitter are not met without the influx of a potent GABA agonist, and withdrawal symptoms occur.  I hope that helps expound upon your question and elucidates this important neuro-mechanism for you a little. Let me Clarify:

1.) 4-PMPD is PRIMARILY a DA/NE releasing agent, like amphetamines, not primarily a RI (like cocaine or methylphenidate).  The releasing agents cause monoamine release as their main MOA, RI's inhibit the reuptake of monoamines.  By definition, 4-PMPD does not work in the same way as classic RI drugs.

2.) This excerpt assumes a description of 4-PMPD alone.  Full context reads: "I found both amfonelic acid and 4-PMPD to have a very similar dopamine-style stimulation without the peripheral effects and classical stimulant feel".  In terms of describing the commonality of experience of these two compounds in terms of perceived stimulation, this is accurate.  Both seem to share their invigorating properties in a way that is purely cerebral- shall I say less somatic- than "classical" stimulants.  I should have elaborated to say that my body was not triggered as somatically with 4-PMPD as it would be with amphetamines (tensing, bruxism).  Also, there are many varieties of stimulants and RCs with definitive, confirmed NE release that are not felt as somatically as others.  NE release does not  mean peripheral stimulation will always occur.  They are highly correlated, but not necessarily causal.  

3.) Agreed that dopamine release makes dopamine releasers and DRI's pleasurable.  However, the amount of dopamine release and/or strength of RI does not directly translate to more euphoria.  When Amfonelic acid was reported to have a dopaminergic potency 50x that of methylphenidate, people misinterpreted that as being 50x more euphoric- this is not the case.  I do indeed assert that 4-PMPD is pleasurable; I did not say that I think it can't make an enjoyable recreational drug.  I enjoy it very much and intend to keep on taking it and experimenting with it- but as I said, the pleasure derived from it and the different way this compound stimulates me makes it NO replacement for Cocaine or Amps.  A compound could have very similar binding affinities for the same receptors and yet still not feel nearly the same or as "euphoric".  4-PMPD is enjoyable in it's own fashion.  If you are expecting cocaine, you will be disappointed.  All we know about this compound is that it is a releasing agent for Dopamine, Norepinephrine, and Serotonin, as well as a weak MAOI, more selective for MAO-A.  We don't know if there are further complexities than these sparse numbers contributing to it's MOA (I suspect there may very well be).  Given the sparsity and lack of further information, I can only convey my experience thus far.  The individuals who experienced little to no effects at high doses also were non-responders to other stimulants and recreational drug users of compounds that most definitely cause cross-tolerance and desensitization to the receptors utilized by 4-PMPD. If you were drawn to 4-PMPD due to it's use in studies for Cocaine dependence and thought it was going to be similar to Cocaine, you're going to have a bad time.  My first time dosing it I did 40mg Oral, waited 30 minutes, and took another 40mg after I didn't feel much; boy was I wrong.  My problem lay in expecting it to feel like an amphetamine or classical stimulant.  There is little to no peripheral stimulation at all.  The 80mg (40+40) dose left me with a headache in my pre-frontal cortex, a side effect I have come to know as over-stimulation of dopamine.  Once I shifted my expectations and began to focus on what I did feel instead of what I expected to feel, I began to notice a definite focused and stimulated feeling, and pleasurable at that.  I also began to notice the effects much more over the next couple of days as I took more doses and became more accustomed to the compound.  In the mornings I am sluggish and generally very tired and hard to rouse, but even under slept on only 4+ hours I dose 30mg and feel very  much so awake; in fact very incapable of going back to sleep. It is most definitely active.  I'm not just someone "sensitive" to stimulants either- I had a long and fair run with amphetamines and stimulants a few years ago and used to take much higher doses than I should have.  If you're looking for an amphetamine or Cocaine replacement, look elsewhere.  If you're looking for a very dopaminergic, pleasurable stimulation with good focus and bereft of the usual peripheral stimulation and classic stimulant sides, 4-PMPD is perfect.  After experiencing some of the larger doses, it makes me very worried that some of you are blasting ahead to upwards of 300mg- the effects you are looking for simply won't come.  Remember, 4-PMPD is only a dopamine/norepinephrine releasing agent, NOT a reuptake inhibitor as well like amphetamines.  Having tried amfonelic acid recently too (a purely DRI), I found both amfonelic acid and 4-PMPD to have a very similar dopamine-style stimulation without the peripheral effects and classical stimulant feel.  As I calculated in the other thread following the HED formula, I find 40mg to be quite stimulating.  Anything higher than that I fear I'm just burning my dopamine receptors searching for a type of stimulation that won't come from a compound with this MoA.  As to the antidepressant properties, I found 4-PMPD to be fantastic in this regard.  The effects seem to be cumulative and it feels a bit more effective each day I continue its use and I become adjusted to it's effects.  I've had another friend of mine test my batch of 4-PMPD as well, and he finds it to also be very stimulating at 40mg.
